result.title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators
result.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation. From a sparse, intermittent measurement window at a few generator buses, the operator estimates the rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines, unmeasured ones included, in one forward pass. A graph-attention encoder processes the measurements, and the swing equations are imposed as a hard constraint or as a soft one with a learned correction that absorbs model errors. It is trained on simulated measurements, without state labels. With several phasor measurement units, masked training hides one from the input but keeps it in the loss. On four transmission systems, simulations show that the operator is the most accurate estimator that neither optimizes per scenario nor uses state labels, except on the smallest system at large model errors, where tuned Kalman smoothers are better. Networks trained on simulated states are more accurate on the two smallest systems but not on the 118-bus system, where the operator is faster and more accurate than hard-constrained moving-horizon estimation. Under model errors, it matches or outperforms an optimization-based benchmark at a fraction of its cost. The results hold for a detailed machine model with exact parameters seen only through voltage phasors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出物理信息图神经算子：从少数发电机母线的稀疏、间歇 PMU 量测出发，单次前向估计全部机组（含未量测机组）的转子角与转速轨迹，以摆方程作硬约束或带可学习误差修正的软约束，并在无状态标签的仿真量测上训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「稀疏观测→全系统隐状态一次推断」及掩码训练（从输入遮蔽一路量测、仍保留在损失中）可能为部分可观测下的 latent 状态估计与监督贡献分配提供线索，可供核查其可迁移性。
